accepted.reason: Good observation-target alignment via delayed_I for hospitalization-rate semantics; minimal added complexity; helps probe whether a shorter lag than the current 2–3 week patterns is plausible without introducing new weakly identifiable compartments.

Matches current discovery pattern (SEIRS/SEIR with delayed_I delay=2) and provides a necessary baseline for interpreting any changes from lag choice vs added structure; observation mapping is plausible for admissions lag and remains identifiable for single-season length.

Still aligned (delayed_I) and low structural risk; delay=3 is plausible per current patterns but may be less responsive for a 31-week single-season series, so keep as a secondary lag-sensitivity check rather than primary.

SEIRS with delayed_I(2) directly tests whether waning immunity adds explanatory power beyond the established lag mapping; however, waning is often weakly identified in short single-season data, so treat as exploratory rather than core.

rejected.reason: Adds waning immunity (SEIRS) while also shifting to a shorter delay=1; with only ~31 training weeks this compounds identifiability/timing tradeoffs (waning can mimic lag/timing shifts), increasing overfitting risk relative to cleaner SEIR lag sweep or SEIRS at the established delay=2.

Combines two smoothing/timing mechanisms (SEIRS + delay=3) in a short single-season series, raising over-complexity and identifiability risk; likely to confound peak timing and amplitude without clear observational support.

Observation-target alignment is conceptually good (H for hospitalizations), but explicit H compartment is flagged as weakly identifiable for short single-season data; parameter tradeoffs (I→H vs H outflow) can create unstable fits/forecasts, making delayed_I more plausible here.

suggested_edits.edit: If this template must be kept, consider switching observation_map from H to I+H (per recommended maps) to reduce reliance on a weakly identifiable standalone H state; otherwise prefer delayed_I for this short single-season series.
To reduce confounding, align with the established lag by changing delay_weeks from 1 to 2 (i.e., make it comparable to proposal_index 4) so the incremental effect is primarily waning vs no waning.
